review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

6:1.sourceText: Συνεργοῦντες δὲ καὶ παρακαλοῦμεν μὴ εἰς κενὸν τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ δέξασθαι ὑμᾶς·
6:1.targetText: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.

groups.note: The participle συνεργοῦντες ("working together") is rendered As … fellow workers.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies God's; the participle says only "working together".

6:2.sourceText: —λέγει γάρ Καιρῷ δεκτῷ ἐπήκουσά σου καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ σωτηρίας ἐβοήθησά σοι· ἰδοὺ νῦν καιρὸς εὐπρόσδεκτος, ἰδοὺ νῦν ἡμέρα σωτηρίας·—
6:2.targetText: For He says:  “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.”   Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders only the first ἰδού ("behold").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

6:3.sourceText: μηδεμίαν ἐν μηδενὶ διδόντες προσκοπήν, ἵνα μὴ μωμηθῇ ἡ διακονία,
6:3.targetText: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.

groups.note: μηδενί ("no one") is rendered anyone's way after the negative.
BSB recasts the passive μὴ μωμηθῇ ("may not be faulted") with the subject no one.
The article ἡ is used as a possessive and rendered our.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies we.
English supplies a subject for the active wording; the Greek verb is passive.

6:4.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ συνιστάνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ὡς Θεοῦ διάκονοι, ἐν ὑπομονῇ πολλῇ, ἐν θλίψεσιν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις, ἐν στενοχωρίαις,
6:4.targetText: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat in before hardships and calamities.

unmappedTarget.reason: A participle has no person; English supplies we.
English joins the last item of the list; the Greek has no καί.

6:5.sourceText: ἐν πληγαῖς, ἐν φυλακαῖς, ἐν ἀκαταστασίαις, ἐν κόποις, ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις, ἐν νηστείαις,
6:5.targetText: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;

groups.note: νηστείαις ("fastings", going without food) is rendered hunger.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat in before imprisonments and riots.
BSB does not repeat in before sleepless nights and hunger.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the last item of the list; the Greek has no καί.
English joins the last item of the list; the Greek has no καί.

6:6.sourceText: ἐν ἁγνότητι, ἐν γνώσει, ἐν μακροθυμίᾳ, ἐν χρηστότητι, ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ, ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἀνυποκρίτῳ,
6:6.targetText: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat in before knowledge, patience and kindness.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the last item of the list; the Greek has no καί.
English joins the two phrases with and; the Greek has no καί.

6:7.sourceText: ἐν λόγῳ ἀληθείας, ἐν δυνάμει Θεοῦ· διὰ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῶν δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν,
6:7.targetText: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;

groups.note: The genitive ἀληθείας ("of truth") is rendered truthful.
The one article τῶν covers both right and left; English repeats it.
The genitive δεξιῶν ("of the right") is rendered in the right hand.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the two phrases with and; the Greek has no καί.

6:8.sourceText: διὰ δόξης καὶ ἀτιμίας, διὰ δυσφημίας καὶ εὐφημίας· ὡς πλάνοι καὶ ἀληθεῖς,
6:8.targetText: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;

groups.note: καί is rendered yet in the contrast.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat through before slander and praise.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds viewed to the comparison; the Greek has only ὡς ("as").

6:9.sourceText: ὡς ἀγνοούμενοι καὶ ἐπιγινωσκόμενοι, ὡς ἀποθνήσκοντες καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶμεν, ὡς παιδευόμενοι καὶ μὴ θανατούμενοι,
6:9.targetText: as unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat as before dying and punished.
BSB leaves ἰδού ("behold") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds on (go on living); ζῶμεν means "we live".

6:10.sourceText: ὡς λυπούμενοι ἀεὶ δὲ χαίροντες, ὡς πτωχοὶ πολλοὺς δὲ πλουτίζοντες, ὡς μηδὲν ἔχοντες καὶ πάντα κατέχοντες.
6:10.targetText: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.

groups.note: πλουτίζοντες ("enriching") is rendered making … rich.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not repeat as in this verse.

6:11.sourceText: Τὸ στόμα ἡμῶν ἀνέῳγεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, Κορίνθιοι, ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν πεπλάτυνται·
6:11.targetText: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.

groups.note: στόμα … ἀνέῳγεν ("mouth has opened") is an idiom rendered have spoken freely.
ἡμῶν ("our", with mouth) becomes the subject We.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

6:12.sourceText: οὐ στενοχωρεῖσθε ἐν ἡμῖν, στενοχωρεῖσθε δὲ ἐν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις ὑμῶν·
6:12.targetText: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.

groups.note: ἡμῖν ("us") is rendered our in BSB's recast.
σπλάγχνοις ("affections") is stated once in English, with our; yours stands for your affection.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB's cleft sentence states restrained once, in the clause about yours.
BSB recasts the ἐν phrases as the possessives our and yours, so ἐν has no English word.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English uses the frame It is … that for emphasis.
English uses the frame It is … that for emphasis.

6:13.sourceText: τὴν δὲ αὐτὴν ἀντιμισθίαν, ὡς τέκνοις λέγω, πλατύνθητε καὶ ὑμεῖς.
6:13.targetText: As a fair exchange, I ask you as my children: Open wide your hearts also.

groups.note: τὴν αὐτὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ("the same recompense", a like-for-like return) is rendered as a unit: As a fair exchange.
λέγω ("I speak") is rendered I ask.
ὑμεῖς ("you") is rendered your with the supplied hearts.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for ask.
English supplies the possessive; the Greek has only τέκνοις ("children").
English supplies hearts from 6:11; the Greek says only "be opened wide".

6:14.sourceText: Μὴ γίνεσθε ἑτεροζυγοῦντες ἀπίστοις· τίς γὰρ μετοχὴ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀνομίᾳ, ἢ τίς κοινωνία φωτὶ πρὸς σκότος;
6:14.targetText: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?

groups.note: καί ("and") joining the two nouns is rendered with.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.

6:15.sourceText: τίς δὲ συμφώνησις Χριστοῦ πρὸς Βελιάρ, ἢ τίς μερὶς πιστῷ μετὰ ἀπίστου;
6:15.targetText: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?

groups.note: πρός ("with") is rendered between … and.
Βελιάρ is another form of the name Belial.
μερίς ("share") is rendered have in common.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an existence verb; the Greek question has none.
English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.

6:16.sourceText: τίς δὲ συνκατάθεσις ναῷ Θεοῦ μετὰ εἰδώλων; ἡμεῖς γὰρ ναὸς Θεοῦ ἐσμεν ζῶντος· καθὼς εἶπεν ὁ Θεὸς ὅτι Ἐνοικήσω ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐνπεριπατήσω, καὶ ἔσομαι αὐτῶν Θεός, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔσονταί μου λαός.
6:16.targetText: What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said:  “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”

groups.note: μετά ("with") is rendered between … and.
αὐτοῖς ("them") is understood again with walk among.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ὅτι introduces the quotation, which BSB marks with a colon and quotation marks.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek question has none.

6:17.sourceText: διὸ ἐξέλθατε ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν, καὶ ἀφορίσθητε, λέγει Κύριος, καὶ ἀκαθάρτου μὴ ἅπτεσθε· κἀγὼ εἰσδέξομαι ὑμᾶς,
6:17.targetText: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”

groups.note: μέσου ("midst") is rendered among.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.

6:18.sourceText: καὶ ἔσομαι ὑμῖν εἰς Πατέρα, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔσεσθέ μοι εἰς υἱοὺς καὶ θυγατέρας, λέγει Κύριος Παντοκράτωρ.
6:18.targetText: And:  “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”

groups.note: ἔσομαι εἰς ("I will be for") is a Semitic idiom for "I will be".
ἔσεσθε εἰς ("you will be for") is a Semitic idiom for "you will be".
